bibl.note: The scanned title identifies Tom. I despite the archive catalogue volume label. One-based viewer pages 116–117 have been inspected; source links are recorded in the facsimile.

normalization.p: Source wording, capitalization, contracted forms and punctuation retained. Typographic ligatures use constituent letters; quotation marks are represented schematically by curly quotes. OCR locates text but does not determine readings.

segmentation.p: Each l corresponds to a printed verse; n preserves the corpus verse identifier. Verses follow the source order, including any transposed couplets, rather than being silently reordered. Each line links to its existing annotation rectangle. Page breaks may occur within couplets. Source headings and running titles are encoded separately.

correction.p: Source readings are not silently replaced by a modern edition. Distinctive features are explained in notes for independent checking.

revisionDesc.change: Independently inspected all 20 actual source verses and every author note. Confirmed source wording, punctuation, marks, page boundaries and actual alternating inset. No human approval implied.

lg.label: XV.
lg.l: Quaere novum vatem, tenerorum mater Amorum:
Raditur hic elegis ultima meta meis;
Quos ego conposui, Paeligni ruris alumnus,
(Nec me deliciae dedecuere meae)
Siquid id est, usque a proavis vetus ordinis heres,
Non modo militiae turbine factus eques.
Mantua Vergilio, gaudet Verona Catullo;
Paelignae dicar gloria gentis ego,
* Quam sua libertas ad honesta coegerat arma,
Cum timuit socias anxia Roma manus.
Atque aliquis spectans hospes Sulmonis aquosi
Moenia, quae campi iugera pauca tenent,
‘Quae tantum’ dicat ‘potuistis ferre poetam,
Quantulacumque estis, vos ego magna voco.’
Culte puer puerique parens Amathusia culti,
Aurea de campo vellite signa meo!
Corniger increpuit thyrso graviore Lyaeus:
Pulsandast magnis area maior equis.
Inbelles elegi, genialis Musa, valete,
Post mea mansurum fata superstes opus!

div.head: Transcription notes
div.note: The source heading is XV. Both full pages show the explicitly recorded alternating insets. A colon follows Amorum.
The source spelling is conposui, with the proper name Paeligni.
The complete printed verse is enclosed in parentheses and has no additional terminal punctuation.
The source prints Siquid as one word and proavis in full.
The source has a comma after Vergilio and a semicolon after Catullo.
A printed asterisk precedes Quam; its function is left unspecified. The verb is coegerat, not replaced from another witness.
The printed quotation is interrupted by dicat outside the quotation. Both pairs of quotation marks across13–14 are represented schematically with curly single quotes.
The source word is Quantulacumque. The full stop follows voco before the closing quotation mark.
The source prints Amathusia culti, retained as read in the enlarged image.
The printed proper name is Lyaeus, followed by a colon.
The printed contraction Pulsandast is retained without expansion.
The source spelling is Inbelles. Commas follow elegi, Musa and valete.
The poem ends with an exclamation mark after opus. The full source page has a short horizontal closing rule and blank space below the final verse; no further poem text follows on this page.
